To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gas chromatography-mass spectroscopy of the monohydrxy acids as their trimethylsilyly ethers is the method of choice for quantitative analysis.

the mass spectra of the monohydoxy acids 5-HETe, 12-HETe and 15-HETE as their methyl estertert.-butyldiethylsilyl ether derivatives are not suitable for quantitative analysis by selected ion monitoring, while the mass spectra of these monohydroxy acid derivatives after reduction of the double bond exhibit very intense ions in the higher mass regions.

the mass spectral fragmentation patterns of the monohydrxy acids 5-HETEs, 12-HETEs and 15-HETEs are very similar and that the mass spectra of the trimethylsilylethers of the methyl ester of 5-Hydroxyeicosanoic acid, 12-Hydroxyeicosaonic acid and 15-Hydroxyeicsanoic acid exhibit intense ions in the high mass range.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the gas chromatographic and the mass spectrometric behaviour of the monohydroy acids and their derivatives, the preparation of the derivatives, the quantitative analysis by selected ion monitoring and the application in biological samples.
the development of a technique that allows a sensitive and selective analysis of the monohydroyeicosatetranenoic acids in biological samples.
the development of a method for the analysis of 5-Hydroxyeicosatrienoic acid, 5-HETT, a recently discovered metabolite of arachidonic acid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methyl ester trimethysilyl ethers are the derivatives of choice for gas chromatography-mass spectral analysis.

the methyl esters trimethysilyl, allydimethylsilyl as well as tert.-butydimethylsily ether derivatives are suitable for gas chromatography-mass specrometry of monobydroxyeicosanoids, but that the trimethylsilly and tert.-butyl dimethlysilyl ether derivatives are preferable.

the trimethylsyl ether of the methyl ester of 12-HETe is the most suitable derivative for gas chromatographic-mass spectrometric measurements of 12-Hydroxyeicosatrienoic acid (HETE) in biological samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trimethylslyl and tert.-butoxymethylsilyl ether derivatives of the monohydrxyeicosatetranoic acid methyl esters are the derivatives of choice for quantitative analysis by selected ion monitoring.
the trimethylslyl and tert.- butyldimethyl silyl ethers are the derivatives of choice for gas chromatography-mass spectroscopy of the monohyd roxy acids.
the trimethylslyl ethers of the monohydric eicosatetraenic acids are excellent derivatives for the gas chromatographic-mass spectrometric analysis of these compounds in biological samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mass spectra of the monohydric acids do not exhibit particularly intense peaks in the upper mass regions.
the mass spectra of the monohydoxy acids do not contain intense ions in the mass region above the molecular ion.
the double bond in the side chain of the hydroxyeicosatetranoic acids is a major determinant of their fragmentation pattern.
